issues.detail: The Hebrew has 'נְחֶמְיָה' (Nehemiah) and 'הַתִּרְשָׁתָא' (the Tirshatha) as two separate titles/names for the same person: 'Nehemiah, he is the Tirshatha'. The Chinese renders '提斯他尼希米雅' which appears to be a garbled conflation, possibly misreading 'הַתִּרְשָׁתָא' as a name '提斯他' and combining it with '尼希米雅', rather than clearly presenting 'Nehemiah the governor'.

The Hebrew has 'וְעֶזְרָא הַכֹּהֵן הַסֹּפֵר' (and Ezra the priest, the scribe). The Chinese renders '與祭司數目以斯拉' which incorrectly translates 'הַסֹּפֵר' (the scribe) as '數目' (number/count), and misplaces '祭司' (priest) before the name, changing the proper title 'Ezra the priest, the scribe' into a garbled phrase.
